text: And also, it is of course important not to then consider it as active unless it is necessary. In particular, it would be great if we can reduce the time spent by the interface in idle mode. Why? Because when you transmit, you are doing something useful, right? You are transmitting data. When you receive data, useful data that is intended for you, that's also useful. But being idle, that means you are doing nothing, and you still consume a lot of power. That's something that you would like to avoid, right? So our one of our goals would be to reduce the time that the interface spends in idle mode. Also, it would be very good, of course, to avoid collisions, to avoid overhead. We know that already. But it will be also very good to avoid the so called overhearing. What does overhearing means? It's when you hear someone else talking, right? When you, for example, you demodulate the header. So in that case, those packets are not intended for you. You are not intended receiver, but you still overhear those packets and demodulate the header, right? So that's something that you would like to avoid because it's a cost. But you are not actually intended receiver for that data packet. So if possible, it would be good to to avoid.
